record.paper_title: A realist view of the electron: recent advances and unsolved problems
record.original_question: In a photon-interaction model of electrostatic fields where charge is expressed through the properties of emitted and absorbed photons and those photons can produce attraction or repulsion, how can the origin of a specific charge or anticharge in a specific situation be comprehensively described?

evidence.quote:
Since,
what might be called charge, ﬁnds its expression in the
properties of the emitted and absorbed photons, and
since these photons can either lead - by way of their
intrinsic properties - to attraction or repulsion of other
charges, the sign of the charge is no longer a quantity
ﬁxed for all time and under every condition. Although
there is, currently, no comprehensive way of describing
the origin of a speciﬁc charge/anticharge in a speciﬁc sit-
uation, it seems that the model should also be suitable
for questions of this type

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a model of electrostatic interactions in which the electromagnetic field between charged particles is mediated entirely by emitted and absorbed photons, and in which the quantity conventionally called "electric charge" of a particle is not a primitive attribute but is instead encoded in the intrinsic properties (e.g. polarization, phase, helicity, or other internal degrees of freedom) of the photons that the particle emits and absorbs. Assume further that, depending on these intrinsic photon properties, the photon exchange between two such particles can give rise either to an attractive or to a repulsive net force. Within this framework, the sign of a particle's charge is therefore not a fixed invariant but a context-dependent quantity determined by the photon-exchange process.

Problem: Provide a comprehensive mathematical description of the origin of a specific charge or anticharge in a specific physical situation within this photon-interaction framework. That is, specify a precise rule or mechanism that, given the intrinsic properties of the emitted and absorbed photons exchanged between two particles in a given configuration, determines the sign and magnitude of the effective charge (or anticharge) attributed to each particle, and explains how attraction versus repulsion arises from these photon properties in a manner consistent with the observed phenomenology of electrostatics.
artifact.status_search_result: No mainstream physics literature was found establishing a comprehensive description of charge/anticharge origin within such a photon-property-based model; the question is speculative and lies outside standard QED, where charge is a conserved quantum number rather than an emergent photon property. Status cannot be verified.
